title: Val Gardena Catalog V2 Fact Enrichment

entity_scope_assessments.rationale: The official destination and directBooking system provide one umbrella Val Gardena stay market across Ortisei, S. Cristina and Selva. Village-level ownership and the missing base graph remain separately unresolved rather than being inferred from the umbrella.
The report's existing official Ortisei evidence supports retaining the current stay-base record while the independent review reconstructs the complete Val Gardena stay-market inventory.

The legacy report did not assess the complete operator, weather-owner, pass, and connected-sector boundary required by schema version 3. The current catalog relationship is retained unchanged for independent source-trust and graph-scope review.

The operator owns a connected consortium presentation and child-scoped terrain operations, but the official inventory gathered here establishes neither an independent weather owner nor a full local pass; under the connected-area test it remains inside the current Val Gardena owner pending reviewer confirmation.

Dantercepies has its own lift operator, schedule and limited three-hour tariff, but no independent weather presentation or full-local-pass owner was established; the official regional map aggregates it into Val Gardena.

The official map and route presentation identify Ciampinoi and Saslong as connected sectors and village gateways, without an independent weather or full-local-pass owner in the reviewed source neighborhood.
The official map and Ronda route identify Monte Pana and Mont de Seura as connected Val Gardena sectors; no independent operations-plus-weather or full-local-pass ownership was established.

The official map and village route describe this as a connected lift sector from Selva and Plan de Gralba; no independent weather or full-local-pass owner was found in the bounded source neighborhood.
The Seceda operator expressly includes Rasciesa in the connected consortium and shared grooming presentation; no independent evidence owner was established.

The map exposes the Passo Gardena presentation, but its complete boundary crosses into the linked Alta Badia graph. It remains deferred until the owning linked graph can establish full operations, weather and pass scope.

The Sella Pass presentation reaches beyond the selected Val Gardena owner graph. Complete membership and parent ownership require the separately owned adjacent regional graph before it can be safely modeled.

The official map and operator establish direct Ortisei-Seceda lift access. Because Seceda remains inside the current Val Gardena area owner, the sector presentation maps to the existing whole-area access edge rather than a second catalog edge.

unresolved_caveats: Official sources confirm snowmaking infrastructure but do not publish a stable child-area coverage percentage with a denominator.
No authoritative glacier, night-skiing, or marked downhill freeride-route inventory was established.
Valley-wide huts and après evidence supports the ski-area profile but is not copied into Ortisei's local après object without base-specific evidence.

Schema-version-3 pre-review normalization preserves the current Val Gardena graph but does not resolve the complete booking, operator, pass, access, or linked-sector candidate inventory; independent source-trust and graph-scope review must do that before remediation.

Stay-market inventory pass 1 establishes one official umbrella booking market and village-specific accommodation views, but independent village ownership and a non-overlapping Ortisei, S. Cristina and Selva destination-or-base graph remain unresolved.

Core-access inventory pass 1 verifies the named official gateways and route sequence, but exact access mode, transfer, directness and source-backed catalog-edge disposition remain missing for Ortisei-Alpe di Siusi, every S. Cristina edge, and every Selva edge.

Operator-boundary inventory pass 1 supports not-separate dispositions for the connected Seceda, Dantercepies, Ciampinoi, Monte Pana, Plan de Gralba and Resciesa presentations; independent weather ownership remains unknown and the Gardena Pass and Sella Pass owner boundaries remain deferred.

The official Seiser Alm evidence establishes a separate 22-lift, 62-km terrain presentation and a separate regional accommodation collection inside the shared pass area, but the complete stay, access, operations/weather-owner and pass graph remains missing and cannot be inferred in this report-only pass.

Plan de Gralba and Monte Pana both have official bookable lodging under Selva and S. Cristina respectively, but pass 1 does not establish whether either is a separate StayBase or a lodging/access sector; no canonical backlog marker currently exists for a schema-valid regional-followup deferral.

Dantercepies publishes a current three-hour ticket for its lift group, but pass 1 does not establish durable trip-planning value or a schema-valid separate-product disposition; no canonical backlog marker currently exists for a regional-followup deferral.
